```{r}
# =============================================================================
# GPS FIX-SUCCESS DIAGNOSTIC
#
# Purpose:
#   Address reviewer/coauthor questions about:
#     1. How many usable GPS fixes occurred per deer per day?
#     2. What proportion of deer-days had 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, or 3 fixes?
#     3. Did fix success differ among individual deer?
#     4. Did fix success differ across seasons/months?
#     5. How much does a >=3 vs >=4 fixes/day criterion affect retention?
#
# IMPORTANT:
#   Run this on data BEFORE 3-hour trajectory regularization.
# =============================================================================


# =============================================================================
# 1. PACKAGES
# =============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)


# =============================================================================
# 2. USER SETTINGS
# =============================================================================

base_dir <- "<LOCAL_PATH>"

neg_file <- file.path(
  base_dir,
  "CWD_negative_training_with_seasons2_copy.csv"
)



pos_file <- file.path(
  base_dir,
  "CWD_positive_testing_with_seasons2_copy.csv"
)

output_dir <- file.path(
  base_dir,
  "GPS_fix_success_diagnostic"
)

dir.create(
  output_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

EXPECTED_FIXES_PER_DAY <- 8
MIN_DAYS <- 20


# =============================================================================
# 3. HELPER: FIND COLUMN NAME
# =============================================================================

find_column <- function(data, candidates, required = TRUE) {

  found <- candidates[candidates %in% names(data)]

  if (length(found) > 0) {

    return(found[1])

  }

  if (required) {

    stop(
      paste0(
        "Could not find any of these columns: ",
        paste(candidates, collapse = ", ")
      )
    )

  }

  return(NA_character_)
}


# =============================================================================
# 4. LOAD DATA
# =============================================================================

cwd_neg <- read_csv(
  neg_file,
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(
    cwd_group = "CWD-"
  )

cwd_pos <- read_csv(
  pos_file,
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(
    cwd_group = "CWD+"
  )

all_data <- bind_rows(
  cwd_neg,
  cwd_pos
)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("DATA LOADED\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

cat("\nTotal rows:", nrow(all_data), "\n")
cat("Unique column<LOCAL_PATH>")
print(names(all_data))


# =============================================================================
# 5. IDENTIFY IMPORTANT COLUMNS
# =============================================================================

id_col <- find_column(
  all_data,
  c(
    "id",
    "ID",
    "deer_id",
    "animal_id"
  )
)

datetime_col <- find_column(
  all_data,
  c(
    "datetime",
    "date_time",
    "DateTime",
    "timestamp",
    "Timestamp",
    "date"
  )
)

dop_col <- find_column(
  all_data,
  c(
    "dop",
    "DOP",
    "dilution_of_precision",
    "DilutionOfPrecision"
  ),
  required = FALSE
)

season_col <- find_column(
  all_data,
  c(
    "season",
    "Season"
  ),
  required = FALSE
)


cat("\nDetected ID column:", id_col, "\n")
cat("Detected datetime column:", datetime_col, "\n")

if (!is.na(dop_col)) {

  cat("Detected DOP column:", dop_col, "\n")

} else {

  cat(
    "WARNING: No DOP column detected.\n",
    "The script cannot independently repeat the DOP <= 10 filter.\n"
  )

}

if (!is.na(season_col)) {

  cat("Detected season column:", season_col, "\n")

} else {

  cat(
    "No season column detected.",
    " Season will be derived from month.\n"
  )

}


# =============================================================================
# 6. STANDARDIZE IMPORTANT VARIABLES
# =============================================================================

all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(

    deer_id = as.character(
      .data[[id_col]]
    ),

    datetime_original =
      as.character(
        .data[[datetime_col]]
      )

  )


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parse datetime
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

all_data$datetime_std <- parse_date_time(
  all_data$datetime_original,
  orders = c(
    "ymd HMS",
    "ymd HM",
    "mdy HMS",
    "mdy HM",
    "Ymd HMS",
    "Ymd HM"
  ),
  tz = "UTC",
  quiet = TRUE
)


cat("\nDatetime parsin<LOCAL_PATH>")
cat(
  "Valid datetime rows:",
  sum(!is.na(all_data$datetime_std)),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Invalid datetime rows:",
  sum(is.na(all_data$datetime_std)),
  "\n"
)


# =============================================================================
# 7. ADD DATE, MONTH, AND SEASON
# =============================================================================

all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(

    fix_date =
      as.Date(datetime_std),

    month =
      month(
        datetime_std,
        label = TRUE,
        abbr = TRUE
      ),

    month_number =
      month(datetime_std)

  )


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Use existing season if present.
# Otherwise derive meteorological season.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (!is.na(season_col)) {

  all_data <- all_data %>%
    mutate(
      season_std =
        as.character(
          .data[[season_col]]
        )
    )

} else {

  all_data <- all_data %>%
    mutate(

      season_std =
        case_when(

          month_number %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",

          month_number %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Spring",

          month_number %in% c(6, 7, 8) ~ "Summer",

          month_number %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Fall",

          TRUE ~ NA_character_

        )
    )

}


# =============================================================================
# 8. EXAMINE DOP FILTERING
# =============================================================================

data_before_dop <- all_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(deer_id),
    !is.na(datetime_std)
  )


if (!is.na(dop_col)) {

  data_before_dop <- data_before_dop %>%
    mutate(
      dop_std =
        suppressWarnings(
          as.numeric(
            .data[[dop_col]]
          )
        )
    )


  cat("\n============================================================\n")
  cat("DOP FILTER SUMMARY\n")
  cat("============================================================\n")

  cat(
    "\nRows before DOP filter:",
    nrow(data_before_dop),
    "\n"
  )

  cat(
    "Rows with DOP > 10:",
    sum(
      data_before_dop$dop_std > 10,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    "\n"
  )

  cat(
    "Rows with missing DOP:",
    sum(
      is.na(data_before_dop$dop_std)
    ),
    "\n"
  )


  # Manuscript states locations with DOP > 10 were removed.
  # Missing DOP values are retained here rather than automatically discarded.

  data_after_dop <- data_before_dop %>%
    filter(
      is.na(dop_std) |
        dop_std <= 10
    )

} else {

  data_after_dop <- data_before_dop

}


cat(
  "\nRows available after DOP filtering:",
  nrow(data_after_dop),
  "\n"
)


# =============================================================================
# 9. COUNT GPS FIXES PER DEER PER DAY
# =============================================================================

daily_fixes <- data_after_dop %>%

  group_by(
    cwd_group,
    deer_id,
    fix_date
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n_fixes =
      n_distinct(datetime_std),

    season =
      first(
        season_std[
          !is.na(season_std)
        ],
        default = NA_character_
      ),

    month =
      first(
        as.character(
          month[
            !is.na(month)
          ]
        ),
        default = NA_character_
      ),

    .groups = "drop"

  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("DAILY FIX COUNTS\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

cat(
  "\nNumber of deer-days:",
  nrow(daily_fixes),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Mean fixes per deer-day:",
  round(
    mean(daily_fixes$n_fixes),
    2
  ),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Median fixes per deer-day:",
  median(daily_fixes$n_fixes),
  "\n"
)


# =============================================================================
# 10. OVERALL FIX-COUNT DISTRIBUTION
# =============================================================================

fix_distribution <- daily_fixes %>%

  mutate(

    fix_category =
      case_when(

        n_fixes >= 8 ~ "8+",

        n_fixes == 7 ~ "7",

        n_fixes == 6 ~ "6",

        n_fixes == 5 ~ "5",

        n_fixes == 4 ~ "4",

        n_fixes == 3 ~ "3",

        n_fixes == 2 ~ "2",

        n_fixes == 1 ~ "1",

        TRUE ~ "0"

      )

  ) %>%

  count(
    fix_category,
    name = "deer_days"
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    percent =
      100 *
      deer_days /
      sum(deer_days)

  )


# Put categories in meaningful order

fix_distribution <- fix_distribution %>%
  mutate(

    fix_category =
      factor(
        fix_category,
        levels = c(
          "1",
          "2",
          "3",
          "4",
          "5",
          "6",
          "7",
          "8+"
        )
      )

  ) %>%
  arrange(
    fix_category
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("OVERALL FIX DISTRIBUTION\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  fix_distribution
)


# =============================================================================
# 11. DIRECT ANSWER TO STEPHANIE'S QUESTION
# =============================================================================

reviewer_summary <- daily_fixes %>%

  summarise(

    total_deer_days =
      n(),

    days_8plus =
      sum(n_fixes >= 8),

    pct_8plus =
      100 * mean(n_fixes >= 8),

    days_7 =
      sum(n_fixes == 7),

    pct_7 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 7),

    days_6 =
      sum(n_fixes == 6),

    pct_6 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 6),

    days_5 =
      sum(n_fixes == 5),

    pct_5 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 5),

    days_4 =
      sum(n_fixes == 4),

    pct_4 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 4),

    days_3 =
      sum(n_fixes == 3),

    pct_3 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 3),

    days_below_4 =
      sum(n_fixes < 4),

    pct_below_4 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes < 4)

  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("REVIEWER-FOCUSED SUMMARY\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  reviewer_summary,
  width = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 12. FIX SUCCESS BY INDIVIDUAL DEER
# =============================================================================

deer_summary <- daily_fixes %>%

  group_by(
    cwd_group,
    deer_id
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n_days =
      n(),

    mean_fixes =
      mean(n_fixes),

    median_fixes =
      median(n_fixes),

    minimum_fixes =
      min(n_fixes),

    maximum_fixes =
      max(n_fixes),

    pct_8plus =
      100 * mean(n_fixes >= 8),

    pct_7plus =
      100 * mean(n_fixes >= 7),

    pct_4 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 4),

    pct_3 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 3),

    pct_below_4 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes < 4),

    .groups = "drop"

  ) %>%

  arrange(
    mean_fixes
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("FIX SUCCESS BY DEER\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  deer_summary,
  n = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 13. FIX SUCCESS BY CWD GROUP
# =============================================================================

cwd_summary <- daily_fixes %>%

  group_by(
    cwd_group
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    deer_days =
      n(),

    unique_deer =
      n_distinct(deer_id),

    mean_fixes =
      mean(n_fixes),

    median_fixes =
      median(n_fixes),

    pct_8plus =
      100 * mean(n_fixes >= 8),

    pct_7plus =
      100 * mean(n_fixes >= 7),

    pct_4 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 4),

    pct_3 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 3),

    pct_below_4 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes < 4),

    .groups = "drop"

  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("FIX SUCCESS BY CWD GROUP\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  cwd_summary,
  width = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 14. FIX SUCCESS BY SEASON
# =============================================================================

season_summary <- daily_fixes %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(season)
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    season
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    deer_days =
      n(),

    unique_deer =
      n_distinct(deer_id),

    mean_fixes =
      mean(n_fixes),

    median_fixes =
      median(n_fixes),

    pct_8plus =
      100 * mean(n_fixes >= 8),

    pct_7plus =
      100 * mean(n_fixes >= 7),

    pct_4 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 4),

    pct_3 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 3),

    pct_below_4 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes < 4),

    .groups = "drop"

  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("FIX SUCCESS BY SEASON\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  season_summary,
  width = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 15. FIX SUCCESS BY MONTH
# =============================================================================

month_summary <- daily_fixes %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(month)
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    month
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    deer_days =
      n(),

    unique_deer =
      n_distinct(deer_id),

    mean_fixes =
      mean(n_fixes),

    median_fixes =
      median(n_fixes),

    pct_8plus =
      100 * mean(n_fixes >= 8),

    pct_4 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 4),

    pct_3 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 3),

    pct_below_4 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes < 4),

    .groups = "drop"

  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("FIX SUCCESS BY MONTH\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  month_summary,
  width = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 16. COMPARE >=3 VS >=4 FIXES PER DAY
# =============================================================================

threshold_comparison <- daily_fixes %>%

  group_by(
    cwd_group,
    deer_id
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    total_observed_days =
      n(),

    days_ge_3 =
      sum(n_fixes >= 3),

    days_ge_4 =
      sum(n_fixes >= 4),

    lost_days_if_4_instead_of_3 =
      days_ge_3 - days_ge_4,

    pct_ge_3 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes >= 3),

    pct_ge_4 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes >= 4),

    eligible_20days_ge3 =
      days_ge_3 >= MIN_DAYS,

    eligible_20days_ge4 =
      days_ge_4 >= MIN_DAYS,

    .groups = "drop"

  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat(">=3 VS >=4 FIXES/DAY COMPARISON\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  threshold_comparison,
  n = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 17. HOW MANY DEER WOULD BE RETAINED?
# =============================================================================

retention_summary <- threshold_comparison %>%

  summarise(

    total_deer =
      n(),

    retained_ge3 =
      sum(eligible_20days_ge3),

    retained_ge4 =
      sum(eligible_20days_ge4),

    deer_lost_using_ge4 =
      retained_ge3 - retained_ge4

  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("INDIVIDUAL RETENTION UNDER EACH RULE\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  retention_summary,
  width = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 18. IDENTIFY DEER WHO CHANGE ELIGIBILITY
# =============================================================================

changed_eligibility <- threshold_comparison %>%

  filter(
    eligible_20days_ge3 !=
      eligible_20days_ge4
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("DEER WHO CHANGE ELIGIBILITY UNDER >=3 VS >=4\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

if (nrow(changed_eligibility) == 0) {

  cat(
    "No deer change eligibility between the >=3 and >=4 rules.\n"
  )

} else {

  print(
    changed_eligibility,
    n = Inf
  )

}


# =============================================================================
# 19. OPTIONAL: DAILY FIX DISTRIBUTION BY CWD GROUP
# =============================================================================

fix_distribution_cwd <- daily_fixes %>%

  mutate(

    fix_category =
      case_when(

        n_fixes >= 8 ~ "8+",

        TRUE ~ as.character(n_fixes)

      )

  ) %>%

  count(
    cwd_group,
    fix_category,
    name = "deer_days"
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    cwd_group
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    percent =
      100 *
      deer_days /
      sum(deer_days)

  ) %>%

  ungroup()


# =============================================================================
# 20. SAVE TABLES
# =============================================================================

write_csv(
  daily_fixes,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "daily_fix_counts.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  fix_distribution,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "overall_fix_distribution.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  reviewer_summary,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "reviewer_summary.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  deer_summary,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "fix_success_by_deer.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  cwd_summary,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "fix_success_by_CWD_group.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  season_summary,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "fix_success_by_season.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  month_summary,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "fix_success_by_month.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  threshold_comparison,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "three_vs_four_fix_threshold.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  changed_eligibility,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "deer_changing_eligibility.csv"
  )
)


# =============================================================================
# 21. PLOT: OVERALL DAILY FIX DISTRIBUTION
# =============================================================================

p1 <- ggplot(
  fix_distribution,
  aes(
    x = fix_category,
    y = percent
  )
) +

  geom_col() +

  theme_bw(
    base_size = 13
  ) +

  labs(

    title =
      "Distribution of Daily GPS Fix Counts",

    x =
      "Usable GPS relocations per deer-day",

    y =
      "Percent of deer-days"

  )


print(p1)


ggsave(
  filename =
    file.path(
      output_dir,
      "daily_fix_distribution.png"
    ),
  plot = p1,
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)


# =============================================================================
# 22. PLOT: FIX SUCCESS BY DEER
# =============================================================================

p2 <- ggplot(
  deer_summary,
  aes(
    x = reorder(
      deer_id,
      mean_fixes
    ),
    y = mean_fixes
  )
) +

  geom_point(
    size = 2
  ) +

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = EXPECTED_FIXES_PER_DAY,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  coord_flip() +

  theme_bw(
    base_size = 12
  ) +

  labs(

    title =
      "Mean Daily GPS Fix Count by Deer",

    x =
      "Deer ID",

    y =
      "Mean usable fixes per day"

  )


print(p2)


ggsave(
  filename =
    file.path(
      output_dir,
      "mean_daily_fixes_by_deer.png"
    ),
  plot = p2,
  width = 8,
  height = 10,
  dpi = 300
)


# =============================================================================
# 23. PLOT: FIX SUCCESS BY SEASON
# =============================================================================

if (nrow(season_summary) > 0) {

  p3 <- ggplot(
    daily_fixes %>%
      filter(
        !is.na(season)
      ),
    aes(
      x = season,
      y = n_fixes
    )
  ) +

    geom_boxplot() +

    geom_hline(
      yintercept =
        EXPECTED_FIXES_PER_DAY,
      linetype = "dashed"
    ) +

    theme_bw(
      base_size = 13
    ) +

    labs(

      title =
        "Daily GPS Fix Counts by Season",

      x =
        "Season",

      y =
        "Usable fixes per deer-day"

    )


  print(p3)


  ggsave(
    filename =
      file.path(
        output_dir,
        "daily_fixes_by_season.png"
      ),
    plot = p3,
    width = 8,
    height = 5,
    dpi = 300
  )

}


# =============================================================================
# 24. FINAL CONSOLE SUMMARY
# =============================================================================

cat("\n\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("FINAL GPS FIX-SUCCESS SUMMARY\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

cat(
  "\nExpected scheduled fixes per day:",
  EXPECTED_FIXES_PER_DAY,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "\nTotal deer-days examined:",
  nrow(daily_fixes),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "\nPercent with >=8 usable fixes:",
  round(
    100 * mean(
      daily_fixes$n_fixes >= 8
    ),
    2
  ),
  "%\n"
)

cat(
  "Percent with exactly 4 usable fixes:",
  round(
    100 * mean(
      daily_fixes$n_fixes == 4
    ),
    2
  ),
  "%\n"
)

cat(
  "Percent with exactly 3 usable fixes:",
  round(
    100 * mean(
      daily_fixes$n_fixes == 3
    ),
    2
  ),
  "%\n"
)

cat(
  "Percent with <4 usable fixes:",
  round(
    100 * mean(
      daily_fixes$n_fixes < 4
    ),
    2
  ),
  "%\n"
)

cat(
  "\nDeer retained with >=20 days at >=3 fixes/day:",
  sum(
    threshold_comparison$eligible_20days_ge3
  ),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Deer retained with >=20 days at >=4 fixes/day:",
  sum(
    threshold_comparison$eligible_20days_ge4
  ),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "\nAll outputs saved t<LOCAL_PATH>",
  output_dir,
  "\n"
)

cat("============================================================\n")

```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)

# ============================================================
# GPS FIX SUCCESS:
# Expected schedule = 8 fixes/day
#
# Calculate proportion of deer-days containing:
# 3/8, 4/8, 5/8, 6/8, 7/8, and 8/8 fixes
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Run AFTER DOP > 10 has been removed
# but BEFORE 3-hour regularization.
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Make sure datetime is recognized
# ------------------------------------------------------------

all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    datetime = as.POSIXct(datetime),
    date = as.Date(datetime)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Count observed fixes for each deer on each day
# ------------------------------------------------------------

daily_fix_counts <- all_data %>%
  group_by(
    id,
    date
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n_fixes = n(),
    season = first(season),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Check for unexpected counts
#
# Because the expected maximum is 8/day, first make sure there
# are not duplicates or days containing >8 fixes.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("CHECK DAILY FIX COUNTS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  daily_fix_counts %>%
    count(n_fixes) %>%
    arrange(n_fixes),
  n = Inf
)


cat(
  "\nDays with >8 fixes:",
  sum(daily_fix_counts$n_fixes > 8),
  "\n"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. OVERALL proportion of days with 3/8 through 8/8 fixes
# ------------------------------------------------------------

overall_fix_success <- daily_fix_counts %>%
  filter(
    n_fixes >= 3,
    n_fixes <= 8
  ) %>%
  count(
    n_fixes,
    name = "n_deer_days"
  ) %>%
  complete(
    n_fixes = 3:8,
    fill = list(n_deer_days = 0)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    total_deer_days_3_to_8 = sum(n_deer_days),
    proportion = n_deer_days / total_deer_days_3_to_8,
    percent = 100 * proportion,
    fix_success = paste0(
      n_fixes,
      "/8"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    fix_success,
    n_fixes,
    n_deer_days,
    proportion,
    percent
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("OVERALL FIX SUCCESS: 3/8 THROUGH 8/8\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  overall_fix_success,
  n = Inf
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. ALSO calculate percentages using ALL observed deer-days
#
# This is important because otherwise days with <3 fixes are
# removed from the denominator.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

total_days <- nrow(daily_fix_counts)

overall_all_days <- daily_fix_counts %>%
  mutate(
    fix_category = case_when(
      n_fixes < 3  ~ "<3/8",
      n_fixes == 3 ~ "3/8",
      n_fixes == 4 ~ "4/8",
      n_fixes == 5 ~ "5/8",
      n_fixes == 6 ~ "6/8",
      n_fixes == 7 ~ "7/8",
      n_fixes == 8 ~ "8/8",
      n_fixes > 8  ~ ">8/8"
    )
  ) %>%
  count(
    fix_category,
    name = "n_deer_days"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percent_all_days =
      100 * n_deer_days / total_days
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("FIX SUCCESS USING ALL DEER-DAYS AS DENOMINATOR\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  overall_all_days,
  n = Inf
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. FIX SUCCESS BY INDIVIDUAL DEER
#
# This directly answers:
# "Did certain deer have better fix success?"
# ------------------------------------------------------------

fix_success_by_deer <- daily_fix_counts %>%
  filter(
    n_fixes >= 3,
    n_fixes <= 8
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    fix_success = paste0(
      n_fixes,
      "/8"
    )
  ) %>%
  count(
    id,
    fix_success,
    name = "n_days"
  ) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(
    total_days = sum(n_days),
    percent = 100 * n_days / total_days
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(
    id,
    fix_success
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("FIX SUCCESS BY INDIVIDUAL DEER\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  fix_success_by_deer,
  n = Inf
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Simpler deer-level summary
#
# Especially useful for identifying deer with poorer fix success.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

deer_summary <- daily_fix_counts %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(

    total_days = n(),

    mean_fixes_per_day =
      mean(n_fixes),

    median_fixes_per_day =
      median(n_fixes),

    pct_8_of_8 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 8),

    pct_7_of_8 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 7),

    pct_6_of_8 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 6),

    pct_5_of_8 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 5),

    pct_4_of_8 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 4),

    pct_3_of_8 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes == 3),

    pct_less_than_3 =
      100 * mean(n_fixes < 3),

    .groups = "drop"

  ) %>%
  arrange(
    mean_fixes_per_day
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("DEER-LEVEL FIX SUCCESS SUMMARY\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  deer_summary,
  n = Inf
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. FIX SUCCESS BY SEASON
#
# This directly answers:
# "Did fix success differ at different times of the year?"
# ------------------------------------------------------------

fix_success_by_season <- daily_fix_counts %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(season),
    n_fixes >= 3,
    n_fixes <= 8
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    fix_success = paste0(
      n_fixes,
      "/8"
    )
  ) %>%
  count(
    season,
    fix_success,
    name = "n_deer_days"
  ) %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  mutate(
    total_deer_days = sum(n_deer_days),
    percent = 100 * n_deer_days / total_deer_days
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("FIX SUCCESS BY SEASON\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  fix_success_by_season,
  n = Inf
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. OPTIONAL: monthly analysis
#
# This is even more detailed than season and can identify
# particular times of year with reduced GPS performance.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

daily_fix_counts <- daily_fix_counts %>%
  mutate(
    month = month(
      date,
      label = TRUE,
      abbr = TRUE
    )
  )


fix_success_by_month <- daily_fix_counts %>%
  filter(
    n_fixes >= 3,
    n_fixes <= 8
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    fix_success = paste0(
      n_fixes,
      "/8"
    )
  ) %>%
  count(
    month,
    fix_success,
    name = "n_deer_days"
  ) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  mutate(
    total_deer_days = sum(n_deer_days),
    percent = 100 * n_deer_days / total_deer_days
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("FIX SUCCESS BY MONTH\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  fix_success_by_month,
  n = Inf
)

# Days with fewer than 3 fixes
low_fix_days <- daily_fix_counts %>%
  filter(n_fixes < 3)

cat("Number of deer-days with <3 fixes:", nrow(low_fix_days), "\n")

print(low_fix_days, n = 50)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# DIAGNOSE WHY DAYS WITH <3 ROWS EXIST
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

# daily_fix_counts should already contain:
# id, date, n_fixes
#
# all_data should contain the rows used to create it.


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Get first and last date for every deer
# ------------------------------------------------------------

deer_date_ranges <- daily_fix_counts %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    first_date = min(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_date  = max(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Identify all days with <3 rows
# ------------------------------------------------------------

low_fix_days <- daily_fix_counts %>%
  filter(n_fixes < 3) %>%
  left_join(
    deer_date_ranges,
    by = "id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    is_first_day = date == first_date,
    is_last_day  = date == last_date,
    boundary_day = is_first_day | is_last_day
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("LOW-FIX DAY DIAGNOSTIC\n")

  "\nTotal days with <3 rows:",

  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Last tracking days:",

  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Either first or last day:",
  sum(low_fix_days$boundary_day),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Internal days with <3 rows:",
  sum(!low_fix_days$boundary_day),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "\nPercent of <3-row days that are tracking boundaries:",
  round(
    100 * mean(low_fix_days$boundary_day),
    2
  ),
  "%\n"
)

# 3. Show distribution: 1 row vs 2 rows
# ------------------------------------------------------------

print(
  low_fix_days %>%
    count(n_fixes) %>%
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# CONFIRM EFFECT OF DOP FILTERING ON DAILY GPS FIX SUCCESS
#
# Goal:
#   Compare number of GPS relocations per deer-day:
#
#   BEFORE DOP filtering
#        vs.
#   AFTER keeping only DOP < 10
#
# This directly tests whether DOP filtering created the
# deer-days with fewer than 3 remaining relocations.
# ============================================================

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)


# ============================================================
# 1. READ ORIGINAL GPS DATA
# ============================================================

file_path <- "<LOCAL_PATH>"

deer_raw <- read_excel(
  file_path,
  sheet = 1,
  .name_repair = "unique"
)


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("RAW DATA\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

cat("Rows:", nrow(deer_raw), "\n")
cat("Unique deer:", n_distinct(deer_raw$AID), "\n")

print(names(deer_raw))


# ============================================================
# 2. RECREATE EARLY CLEANING FROM ORIGINAL PREPROCESSING
#
# Original preprocessing removed missing coordinates BEFORE
# applying the DOP criterion.
# ============================================================

deer_clean <- deer_raw %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Latitude),
    !is.na(Longitude)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    AID = as.character(AID),

    DOP = as.numeric(DOP),

    datetime = as.POSIXct(
      Date_Time,
      format = "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M"
    ),

    date = as.Date(datetime)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(AID),
    !is.na(datetime)
  )


cat("\nRows after removing missing coordinates:",
    nrow(deer_clean), "\n")


# ============================================================
# 3. COUNT FIXES/DAY BEFORE DOP FILTERING
# ============================================================

before_dop <- deer_clean %>%
  group_by(
    AID,
    date
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    fixes_before = n_distinct(datetime),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ============================================================
# 4. APPLY EXACT DOP FILTER USED IN PREPROCESSING
#
# Your original code was:
#
#     filter(DOP < 10)
#
# Therefore DOP >= 10 is removed.
# ============================================================

deer_after_dop <- deer_clean %>%
  filter(
    DOP < 10
  )


after_dop <- deer_after_dop %>%
  group_by(
    AID,
    date
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    fixes_after = n_distinct(datetime),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ============================================================
# 5. JOIN BEFORE AND AFTER
#
# A day that completely disappears after DOP filtering should
# have fixes_after = 0.
# ============================================================

daily_comparison <- before_dop %>%
  left_join(
    after_dop,
    by = c("AID", "date")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    fixes_after = replace_na(fixes_after, 0L),

    fixes_removed =
      fixes_before - fixes_after,

    pct_fixes_retained =
      100 * fixes_after / fixes_before
  )


# ============================================================
# 6. BASIC CHECK
# ============================================================

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("DAILY GPS FIX COUNTS BEFORE VS AFTER DOP FILTERING\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

cat("\nTotal deer-days:", nrow(daily_comparison), "\n")

cat(
  "Days losing >=1 fix because of DOP:",
  sum(daily_comparison$fixes_removed > 0),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Percent of days losing >=1 fix:",
  round(
    100 * mean(daily_comparison$fixes_removed > 0),
    2
  ),
  "%\n"
)

cat(
  "Total GPS fixes removed by DOP filter:",
  sum(daily_comparison$fixes_removed),
  "\n"
)


# ============================================================
# 7. CRITICAL QUESTION:
# HOW MANY DAYS HAVE <3 FIXES AFTER DOP FILTERING?
# ============================================================

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("DAYS WITH <3 FIXES AFTER DOP FILTERING\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

low_after_dop <- daily_comparison %>%
  filter(
    fixes_after < 3
  )


cat(
  "\nNumber of days with <3 fixes after DOP filtering:",
  nrow(low_after_dop),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Percent of all deer-days:",
  round(
    100 * nrow(low_after_dop) / nrow(daily_comparison),
    2
  ),
  "%\n"
)


# ============================================================
# 8. WERE THOSE DAYS >=3 BEFORE DOP FILTERING?
#
# THIS IS THE BIG TEST.
# ============================================================

low_day_origin <- low_after_dop %>%
  mutate(

    had_at_least_3_before =
      fixes_before >= 3,

    dropped_below_3_due_to_dop =
      fixes_before >= 3 &
      fixes_after < 3

  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("DID DOP FILTERING CREATE THE <3-FIX DAYS?\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

cat(
  "\n<3-fix days that originally had >=3 fixes:",
  sum(low_day_origin$dropped_below_3_due_to_dop),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Percent of <3-fix days explained by DOP filtering:",
  round(
    100 *
      mean(
        low_day_origin$dropped_below_3_due_to_dop
      ),
    2
  ),
  "%\n"
)


# ============================================================
# 9. EXACT BEFORE -> AFTER TRANSITIONS
#
# This is probably the most useful table.
#
# Examples:
#
#   8 -> 8
#   8 -> 7
#   8 -> 6
#   ...
#   8 -> 2
#   8 -> 1
# ============================================================

transition_table <- daily_comparison %>%
  count(
    fixes_before,
    fixes_after,
    name = "n_deer_days"
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    fixes_before
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percent_within_before =
      100 * n_deer_days / sum(n_deer_days)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(
    fixes_before,
    desc(fixes_after)
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("FIX COUNT TRANSITIONS: BEFORE -> AFTER DOP\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  transition_table,
  n = Inf
)


# ============================================================
# 10. SPECIFICALLY EXAMINE DAYS THAT STARTED WITH 8 FIXES
# ============================================================

eight_fix_days <- daily_comparison %>%
  filter(
    fixes_before == 8
  ) %>%
  count(
    fixes_after,
    name = "n_deer_days"
  ) %>%
  complete(
    fixes_after = 0:8,
    fill = list(
      n_deer_days = 0
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percent =
      100 *
      n_deer_days /
      sum(n_deer_days),

    category =
      paste0(
        fixes_after,
        "/8"
      )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    fixes_after
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("DAYS THAT ORIGINALLY HAD 8/8 FIXES\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  eight_fix_days,
  n = Inf
)


# ============================================================
# 11. DISTRIBUTION BEFORE DOP
# ============================================================

before_distribution <- before_dop %>%
  count(
    fixes_before,
    name = "n_deer_days"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percent =
      100 *
      n_deer_days /
      sum(n_deer_days)
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("DAILY FIX DISTRIBUTION BEFORE DOP FILTERING\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  before_distribution,
  n = Inf
)


# ============================================================
# 12. DISTRIBUTION AFTER DOP
# ============================================================

after_distribution <- daily_comparison %>%
  count(
    fixes_after,
    name = "n_deer_days"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percent =
      100 *
      n_deer_days /
      sum(n_deer_days)
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("DAILY FIX DISTRIBUTION AFTER DOP FILTERING\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  after_distribution,
  n = Inf
)


# ============================================================
# 13. LOOK SPECIFICALLY AT THE PROBLEMATIC DAYS
# ============================================================

problem_days <- daily_comparison %>%
  filter(
    fixes_after < 3
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    fixes_after,
    desc(fixes_before)
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("ALL DAYS WITH <3 FIXES AFTER DOP FILTERING\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  problem_days,
  n = Inf
)


# ============================================================
# 14. SUMMARY BY DEER
#
# Determine whether certain deer were disproportionately
# affected by poor DOP.
# ============================================================

dop_by_deer <- daily_comparison %>%
  group_by(
    AID
  ) %>%
  summarise(

    n_days =
      n(),

    fixes_before =
      sum(fixes_before),

    fixes_after =
      sum(fixes_after),

    fixes_removed =
      sum(fixes_removed),

    pct_removed =
      100 *
      fixes_removed /
      fixes_before,

    days_below_3_after =
      sum(fixes_after < 3),

    pct_days_below_3_after =
      100 *
      mean(fixes_after < 3),

    .groups = "drop"

  ) %>%
  arrange(
    desc(pct_days_below_3_after)
  )


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("DOP EFFECT BY DEER\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  dop_by_deer,
  n = Inf
)

```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# TEST HYPOTHESIS:
# Require >=3 original fixes/day BEFORE applying DOP < 10
# ============================================================

# 1. Identify days that originally had at least 3 fixes
eligible_days_before_dop <- before_dop %>%
  filter(fixes_before >= 3) %>%
  select(AID, date)

# 2. Restrict raw cleaned GPS data to those eligible days
deer_ge3_before_dop <- deer_clean %>%
  semi_join(
    eligible_days_before_dop,
    by = c("AID", "date")
  )

# 3. Now apply the actual DOP criterion
deer_ge3_after_dop <- deer_ge3_before_dop %>%
  filter(DOP < 10)

# 4. Count remaining fixes per day
ge3_then_dop <- eligible_days_before_dop %>%
  left_join(
    deer_ge3_after_dop %>%
      group_by(AID, date) %>%
      summarise(
        fixes_after_dop = n_distinct(datetime),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = c("AID", "date")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    fixes_after_dop = replace_na(fixes_after_dop, 0L)
  )

# 5. Distribution after BOTH rules
distribution_ge3_then_dop <- ge3_then_dop %>%
  count(
    fixes_after_dop,
    name = "n_deer_days"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percent =
      100 * n_deer_days / sum(n_deer_days)
  )

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("IF >=3 FIXES WAS REQUIRED BEFORE DOP FILTERING\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

print(
  distribution_ge3_then_dop,
  n = Inf
)

cat(
  "\nDays originally eligible (>=3 fixes):",
  nrow(ge3_then_dop),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Eligible days subsequently falling below 3 after DOP:",
  sum(ge3_then_dop$fixes_after_dop < 3),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Percent falling below 3 because of DOP:",
  round(
    100 * mean(ge3_then_dop$fixes_after_dop < 3),
    3
  ),
  "%\n"
)
```

### Final answer regarding pings
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

# ============================================================
# Ping-threshold sensitivity table
#
# Use this AFTER DOP filtering and after your final cleaned
# telemetry dataset is created.
# ============================================================

# Update these if your column names differ
id_col <- "id"
datetime_col <- "date_time"

# Replace all_data with the dataframe you are analyzing
ping_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    date_time_tmp = as.POSIXct(.data[[datetime_col]]),
    date = as.Date(date_time_tmp)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(.data[[id_col]]),
    !is.na(date)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Count pings per deer-day
# ------------------------------------------------------------
daily_ping_counts <- ping_data %>%
  group_by(
    id = .data[[id_col]],
    date
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    pings_per_day = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

total_deer_days <- nrow(daily_ping_counts)
total_points <- sum(daily_ping_counts$pings_per_day)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Simple distribution table
# ------------------------------------------------------------
ping_distribution <- daily_ping_counts %>%
  count(
    pings_per_day,
    name = "deer_days"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percent_deer_days = round(deer_days / total_deer_days * 100, 2),
    gps_points = pings_per_day * deer_days,
    percent_gps_points = round(gps_points / total_points * 100, 2)
  ) %>%
  arrange(pings_per_day)

print(ping_distribution)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Threshold sensitivity table
# What would be dropped if we required at least N pings/day?
# ------------------------------------------------------------
threshold_table <- tibble(
  minimum_required_pings_per_day = c(3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8)
) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    deer_days_dropped =
      sum(daily_ping_counts$pings_per_day < minimum_required_pings_per_day),

    percent_deer_days_dropped =
      round(deer_days_dropped / total_deer_days * 100, 2),

    gps_points_dropped =
      sum(daily_ping_counts$pings_per_day[
        daily_ping_counts$pings_per_day < minimum_required_pings_per_day
      ]),

    percent_gps_points_dropped =
      round(gps_points_dropped / total_points * 100, 2),

    deer_days_retained =
      sum(daily_ping_counts$pings_per_day >= minimum_required_pings_per_day),

    percent_deer_days_retained =
      round(deer_days_retained / total_deer_days * 100, 2),

    gps_points_retained =
      sum(daily_ping_counts$pings_per_day[
        daily_ping_counts$pings_per_day >= minimum_required_pings_per_day
      ]),

    percent_gps_points_retained =
      round(gps_points_retained / total_points * 100, 2)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

print(threshold_table)
```
